Cell Covers (CC) 

Aisha worked for several years for a company that repairs mobile (cell) phones in country Z. She had always wanted to be her own boss and decided to leave her job to set up CC to produce covers for mobile phones. She went into partnership with her brother, Aruna. He worked as an Operations Manager for a company producing children’s clothes. 

The sources of finance for the business were \$10 000 of savings from each partner and a bank loan of \$10 000. CC was also given a government grant to help the new business get started. CC leased a factory, bought some equipment and had to pay some expenses before the business had regular cash inflows. 

CC’s current product is a range of standardised phone covers which are sold in the mass market. These are sold using a competitive pricing method through mobile phone shops. CC employs 10 skilled production workers who are paid just above the legal minimum wage. These workers have been trained how to operate the equipment and work as a team on the production line. During the production process there is a lot of waste plastic produced and CC sends this to landfill sites. The business has just completed its second year of trading. 

CC is about to launch a new range of individual personalised phone covers. It will need to recruit 2 additional production workers. Aruna knows that the marketing mix for this new product may have to be different to the marketing mix used for the standardised products. The new product will be aimed at a niche market of high income consumers between the ages of 18 to 25. There are few other competitors in this market at present.

{align=center} **Appendix 1 **

{align=center} **Newspaper article in Main News**

Country Z has been in a recession but the economy is now  growing rapidly and unemployment is falling. With higher incomes the majority of people now own a mobile phone. This makes communication easier. Mobile banking is becoming more popular and it is used by a large percentage of the population.

{align=center} **Appendix 2 **

{align=center} **Advertisement for CC’s standardised mobile phone covers**

Do you want to protect your phone from damage? Then buy a phone cover from CC. Your phone will never be damaged if you use one of our high quality covers!! 

We offer a range of standardised covers at competitive prices. The CC range has many different colours and designs so you will stand out from the crowd.

{align=center} **Appendix 3 **

{align=center} **Summary of CC’s financial information from the end of the second year of trading (\$)**

{align=center} 

| Revenue | 800 000 |
| --- | ---: |
| Cost of sales | 400 000 |
| Gross profit | 400 000 |
| Expenses | 250 000 |
| Profit | 150 000 |
| Current Assets | 20 000 |
| of which: Inventory | 5 000 |
| Current liabilities | 15 000 |

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of the following **three **methods of employee selection. Which method should CC use when recruiting production workers? Justify your answer.

- Application form
- Interview
- Aptitude tests

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2020-paper-22-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
Application forms provide detailed information for comparing candidates' qualifications to operate CC's new production equipment **[Ap]**. However, reviewing forms is time-consuming, and applicants may not be entirely truthful about their skills, which may lead to CC appointing the wrong applicant **[An]**

Interviews allow Aisha to assess applicants' personalities face-to-face. This is crucial, as CC needs team players to work alongside the existing ten production line workers **[Ap]**. Interviews also let applicants ask questions, ensuring they understand the job requirements before they accept the job **[An]**. However, they do not allow candidates to demonstrate practical production line skills **[An]**

Aptitude tests show if applicants can perform the job effectively, which is important for operating CC's machinery efficiently **[An]** . They can show how well candidates interact with the other skilled workers **[Ap]**. However, they may not reveal an applicant's ability to learn skills for CC's new production process **[Ap] **which is likely to be somewhat different to allow for personalisation** [Ap]**

CC should use interviews as the primary selection method **[E]**. This will allow them to assess teamwork skills and explain the requirements for producing both standardised and new personalised phone covers **[Ap]**. As the involve face-to-face interaction, Aisha may find interviews an effective way to identify workers who will fit into CC's factory environment, collaborate well with current employees, and contribute to efficient production **[E]** as the business grows **[Ap]**. This is not possible with a written application form **[An]**. As aptitude tests may not reveal an applicant's ability to learn new skills for the different production processes CC intends to introduce, they will not give Aisha all of the information she needs to make the best choice  **[E]**

> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Application form**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Wide range of written information on each applicant **→** quicker first screen than interviewing everyone
>     - Forms can be laid side-by-side **→** makes it easier to compare candidates fairly
>     - Lists qualifications needed to run the machines **→** CC can see straight away who is trainable
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Takes time to read every form **→** slows the hiring process
>     - Applicants can exaggerate or lie **→** risk of short-listing the wrong people
> - **Interview**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Face-to-face meeting shows personality **→** judge whether the candidate will fit into a production-line team
>     - Lets managers test teamwork and communication skills **→** higher future motivation
>     - Applicants can ask questions **→** lowers the chance they quit soon after hiring
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - More time-consuming and costly than reading forms
>     - Confident talkers may impress even if their skills are weak **→** possibility of a poor hire
> - **Aptitude test**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Measures practical ability to operate equipment **→** candidates cannot fake skill
>     - Helps pick the most skilful worker **→** higher productivity and lower unit costs
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Tests can be expensive and time-consuming to design and run
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Application forms: a cheap, written record for easy comparison, but the information can be false and takes time to read
>   - Interviews: reveal personality and team fit, yet they are slower and may favour confident speakers over truly skilled workers
>   - Aptitude tests: hard proof of machine-handling skills, but they add cost and extend the recruitment timeline
>   - A balanced approach could be: application forms for short-listing → brief interviews for team fit → a short aptitude test before the final offer to combine speed, fairness and reliability

{align=center} **Safari Adventures (SA) **

Tokumbo is a sole trader. He started SA 2 years ago in country X. Tokumbo had previously worked for a company selling holidays. SA organises safari tours which take tourists to view wild animals on a game reserve. Most of SA’s customers are tourists from other countries. Tokumbo did not have any objectives when he started SA but knows they are important for his business. 

SA uses its own vehicles for the 7 day safari tours and provides accommodation in small local hotels. Tokumbo employs 4 safari guides, 1 for each of the 4 vehicles. The safari guides drive the tourists around the game reserve. There is 1 additional employee who helps Tokumbo in the office with administration. Tokumbo thinks SA needs a website so tourists can book directly with them rather than booking through holiday companies that charge SA a fee. 

Tokumbo is considering the following three options for the future growth of SA safari tours: 

- Option 1 - increasing the number of safari guides and vehicles to increase the number of customers from the existing target market
- Option 2 – targeting young people who want to camp and sleep in a tent on their safari
- Option 3 - targeting high-income tourists who prefer to stay in luxury hotels

Information about these three options is outlined in Appendix 3. 

Tokumbo plans to provide more training for his employees whichever option he chooses. He wants his existing employees to have a wider knowledge of the wild animals on the game reserve and to be able to provide high-quality customer service. Tokumbo has to decide which method of training to use.

{align=center} **Appendix 1 **

{align=center} **Newspaper article in Main News, September 2022 **

{align=center} **Tourism takes off**

Country X is becoming a popular holiday destination for tourists from other countries.

There is an increased demand from high-income tourists who want to stay in luxury hotels whilst on safari tours. These tourists are willing to pay high prices. There is also a new trend for younger people who want cheaper holidays. They prefer to camp and sleep in tents on game reserves rather than stay in hotels. 

Are the many safari businesses in country X ready to target these new markets? 

The use of e-commerce to find and book safari tours by tourists from other countries is offering both opportunities and threats to businesses in country X. 

The inflation rate in country X has increased to 4% which may affect some of our local safari businesses.

{align=center} **Appendix 2 **

{align=center} **Email from Tokumbo’s accountant**

To: Tokumbo 

From: Accountant 

Subject: Source of finance for the new vehicles 

New vehicles will be needed whichever option you choose for the future growth of your business. 

I have considered several sources of finance you could use for the new vehicles. Interest rates on bank loans have fallen to 2% whilst interest rates on savings are 3%. I think you should choose from one of the following sources: 

- Leasing
- Bank loan
- Retained profit

We can meet to discuss these sources if that would help you to decide.

{align=center} **Appendix 3 **

{align=center} **SA’s three options for a 7 day safari tour**

|   | Option 1 More existing safari tours | Option 2 Camping safari tours | Option 3 Luxury safari tours |
| --- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Forecast number of tourists per week | 16 | 32 | 10 |
| Total costs per week for SA to provide these safari tours | \$12 000 | \$8000 | \$20 000 |
| Average cost per tourist | \$750 | ? | ? |
| Price per tourist | \$1000 | \$400 | \$2400 |

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of two methods of training Tokumbo could use for his existing employees. Which method should he use? Justify your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2022-paper-21-case-study---new.pdf)[ ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2021-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
On-the-job training is specific to SA's safari tours, so employees learn exactly what they need to know about the animals **[Ap] **and customer service **[An]**. It's usually cheaper than off-the-job training because existing staff can provide the training. Also, safari tours **[Ap] **could include trainees as they learn while working, so SA would not miss out on revenue. However, the trainer might pass on bad habits, which could lead to safety concerns for tourists **[An]**

Off-the-job training involves experts providing training, so employees learn up-to-date information about game reserve species **[Ap]**. This could give SA an edge over competitors, as tour guides would be well informed, able to answer questions about habitats and conservation **[An]**. Training in the evening, could avoid losing tours during the day. However, while training, employees are paid but not working, which increases business costs **[An]**

Tokumbo should use on-the-job training because SA's employees will develop skills specific to SA's safari tours **[E]**. Off-the-job training might be more expensive and less focused on SA's needs **[E]**. On-the-job training will help Tokumbo's employees provide better service to tourists, which is crucial for the success of his safari business **[E]**, especially as it is facing increasing competition** [Ap]**

>   - **Advantages**

{align=center} **Cherished Chocolates (CC)**

CC is a public limited company. It employs 4000 workers in country X and many are members of a trade union. CC has manufactured chocolate bars in country X for 50 years. It imports most of its raw materials, such as cocoa beans. Over the last 10 years CC has expanded and now sells in other countries. Many of these countries have no trade restrictions. The Directors of CC know that globalisation has opportunities and threats for CC. 

CC produces a number of brands of chocolate bars, such as Tiabar, in country X. Its most popular chocolate bar, Choco, has the highest market share. The total market for chocolate bars is no longer growing in country X. CC plans to reduce the number of brands it sells in country X. It has to decide which of the two brands shown in Appendix 1 to stop selling. 

NM operates in country Z and sells its own brands of chocolate bars, including Nuttybar. NM employs 500 workers. In country Z chocolate bars are distributed through small retail outlets. The wage rates in country Z are lower than in country X. However, incomes in country Z are starting to rise. 

The Directors of CC are planning to take over NM to expand into this market rather than setting up a factory. The takeover will cost \$35 million, some of which will be financed by a bank loan. The shareholders of NM are being offered CC shares in exchange for NM shares. 

The Directors of CC know there might be diseconomies of scale after the takeover. They also have to decide who will be the Operations Manager for NM’s factory in country Z. They could keep NM’s existing Operations Manager or move CC’s Operations Manager from country X. Information about the two managers is shown in Appendix 2.

{align=center} **Appendix 1 **

{align=center} **The product life cycles of two of CC’s brands of chocolate bars in country X**

**Option 1 – stop producing Tiabar **

A brand aimed at young children which is a new target market for CC. The market research at the development stage showed positive results from test marketing and sales have been growing steadily. There are many multinational chocolate bar companies targeting this age group. 

**Option 2 – stop producing Choco** 

The market leader in country X. It is a well established brand targeting adults. Sales are high but have not been increasing for several years. No new competitors have entered this market in the last two years.

Ritesh already works in country Z **[Ap]**, so he understands the local market and business environment. This local knowledge could help CC successfully expand into country Z, where chocolate bars **[Ap]**are distributed through small retail outlets **[An]**. Ritesh also has experience working for a chocolate company in country Z **[Ap]**, which gives him useful insights into competitors. Additionally, he has existing relationships with local suppliers, which could help CC establish its operations there **[An]**

Samuel has worked at CC for 20 years **[Ap] **and thoroughly understands CC's production methods, brands, and company culture. This deep knowledge of CC would allow him to effectively implement CC's practices at the NM factory **[An]**. Samuel also has established relationships with CC's high-quality ingredient suppliers **[Ap]**, which could help maintain product quality **[An]**

On balance, I recommend choosing Ritesh for the role **[E]**. His local knowledge and experience in country Z will be invaluable as CC expands into this new market **[Ap]**. While Samuel knows CC's operations well, Ritesh's understanding of country Z's business environment, competitors, and supply chains is likely to be more important for successfully integrating NM's operations **[E]**. Ritesh can learn CC's methods over time, but Samuel would take much longer to gain Ritesh's local expertise **[E]**. Although Samuel's experience with CC is valuable, it is less critical than Ritesh's local knowledge for this specific role in a new market **[E]**

TT is a large manufacturer of toys based in country Y. It is a public limited company and has been trading for 20 years. TT’s products are designed for children up to the age of 5. 

TT has benefited from economies of scale as it has grown. The company has been able to buy specialist new equipment for the flow production line in its factory. parts.problem_md: Do you think an organisation should always use external recruitment when recruiting skilled employees? Justify your answer.
parts.solution_md:
External recruitment provides a wider pool of applicants for a business to select the candidate with the most attractive range of new skills, experience and ideas to work in the business **[K]**. This may help a business become more innovative, efficient and competitive, as these skills and characteristics help a business to develop. **[An]**

Internal recruitment can motivate existing staff by offering promotion opportunities **[K]**. This could lead to better employee retention and reduced absenteeism, reducing business costs **[An]**

The best approach to recruitment depends on the specific situation **[E]**. If the required skills don't exist within the company, external recruitment is necessary. However, if suitable candidates are available internally, this could be quicker and more cost-effective **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include
> 
>   - External recruitment:
>   
>     - Bring in new skills / ideas [k] which could help improve productivity /effectiveness / efficiency of business [an]
>     - Can bring in valuable knowledge and experience of competition [k] gaining a competitive edge [an]
>     - Wider choice of applicants [k] increases possibility of finding best person for job [an]
>     - No knowledge of how business works / current operations [k] so might need induction training [an]
>     - Avoids risk of upsetting employees when someone internal is promoted [k]
>     - Higher recruitment costs [k]
>     - More time spent / takes longer to fill vacancy [k]
>     - Required if no suitable candidates in the business [k]
>   - Internal recruitment :
>   
>     - Can help motivate other employees [k] which could lead to fewer people leaving / reduce absenteeism [an]
>     - Internal promotion can create another vacancy that then needs to be filled [k]
>   - Other appropriate responses should also be credited
>   - Justification might include:
>   
>     - External recruitment can bring in new skills and ideas [k] helping improve productivity [an]. Whereas using internal recruitment can help motivate other employees [k] which could lead to fewer people leaving [an]. Overall, it depends on the skills within the business because if there are no suitable workers external recruitment would be the only choice. [eval] [eval]
> - For evaluation to be awarded justification will usually follow on from relevant analysis of points
> - Advantages of external recruitment can be disadvantages of internal but do not award the same point twice as mirror answers are not accepted

parts.problem_md: Explain **four **effects of training on a business.
parts.solution_md:
Training can increase employee motivation **[K]**. When workers learn new skills, they often feel more valued and work harder** [An]**

Training can improve productivity **[K]**. Employees who know how to do their jobs well can complete tasks faster and with fewer mistakes **[An]**

Training can lead to better quality products or services **[K]**. Well-trained staff are more likely to meet customer needs by producing high quality work **[An]**

Training can create a more flexible workforce **[K]**. Employees who have a wider range of skills can be moved between different tasks as needed **[An]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - In your answer:
> 
>   - Give four valid reasons related to the question → 4 K marks
>   - For each reason, explain how or why it matters using a cause–effect link → 4 An marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Relevant effects might include:
> 
>   - Greater motivation of employees – work harder to produce output
>   - More flexible workforce – employees can be moved between tasks as necessary
>   - Increased productivity/efficiency – lower unit costs
>   - Quality of the product may be improved – greater customer satisfaction /improved brand image / improved reputation
>   - Employees able to use new technology – easier to introduce new equipment to speed up production
>   - Improves customer service – if trained how to answer customer queries
>   - Fewer mistakes as employees are trained – less waste/less repair costs
>   - Workforce is more knowledgeable/skilled – able to complete tasks more effectively
>   - Output lost whilst training employees – higher costs
>   - Employees may expect higher pay increasing wage costs as a result of being trained – lower motivation if pay is not increased
>   - Training costs are incurred by the business – higher costs for the business may lead to lower profit initially
>   - Employees may leave the business after they have been trained – therefore increases recruitment costs

parts.problem_md: Do you think it is better for a tertiary sector business to use full-time employees rather than part-time employees? Justify your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Full-time workers are often more familiar with the business **[K]**, which helps build customer relationships in stores or call centres, and improves the company's reputation. It's usually easier to communicate with full-time staff, leading to fewer errors and misunderstandings, which is likely to lead to more consistent customer service **[An]**

On the other hand, part-time employees allow businesses to extend their hours and cover busy periods flexibly **[K]**, minimising labour costs as the business only pays for hours these staff have actually worked **[An]**

Overall, I believe full-time employees are better for a tertiary sector business **[E] **because consistent service is crucial for customer loyalty. As quality of service is how customers often judge these businesses, having dedicated full-time staff is more likely to ensure repeat customers and maintain sales **[E]**

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

{align=center} **Gemma’s Jewels (GJ)**

Gemma set up GJ as a sole trader 5 years ago in country Z. She started by selling rings and bracelets from a rented shop. She used her own savings to start the business. The first year was successful. After this first year Gemma decided to expand by selling more expensive items of jewellery. Gemma thinks it is important to set clear business objectives. She wants her business to increase sales by 10% each year and to increase market share.

As the business grew Gemma needed more finance for a computer, inventory and working capital to avoid liquidity problems. She decided to convert the business to a private limited company and sell shares to members of her family. Gemma still owns more than 50% of the shares in GJ.

In 2019, Gemma purchased a franchise from Beautywise Jewellery. This means GJ is now only able to sell Beautywise products in its shop. GJ has to purchase all of its inventory from Beautywise and in addition pay 20% of gross profit to Beautywise. More details about the franchise are in the advertisement in Appendix 1.

Gemma has developed a website so customers can order online. Customers can also download a mobile (cell) phone app to view and order jewellery.

Gemma plans to open a second shop as a Beautywise franchise in a nearby town. She has to decide which method of sales promotion to use. GJ needs to recruit a manager for the new shop. The manager will be responsible for operating the shop and making most of the decisions about which items of inventory to buy. The manager will also need to ensure excellent customer service is provided and that the new employees are motivated and working efficiently.

{align=center} **Appendix 1 **

{align=center} **Advertisement for Beautywise Jewellery Franchise**

**Become a franchisee to sell Beautywise Jewellery and improve your chances of success!!**

What we offer you:

- Be the only shop in your area that sells Beautywise jewellery
- Beautywise will advertise nationally on television and in newspapers
- Help and advice on decoration of the shop and training for employees and the franchisee
- Ethically sourced jewellery imported especially for Beautywise
- The franchise fee is just \$50 000 per year!

{align=center} **Appendix 2 **

{align=center} **Newspaper article- Daily News **

**External factors affecting the jewellery market in country Z**

The demand for jewellery in country Z is likely to be affected by some recent changes. Consumers are becoming more aware of the ethical issues involved in jewellery production in some countries. The exchange rate of the currency of country Z is likely to depreciate over the next 12 months. The Government is planning changes to tax rates which might reduce the effects of the current economic boom.

{align=center} **Appendix 3 **

{align=center} **Information on three possible locations for the new shop**

| **Annual costs** | **Town A** | **Town B** | **Town C** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shop rent | \$45 000 per year for 5 years | \$35 000 per year for 10 years | \$20 000 per year for 15 years |
| Wages and salaries | \$80 000 | \$70 000 | \$60 000 |
| Heating and lighting | \$5 000 | \$5 000 | \$3 000 |
| Estimated gross profit | \$400 000 | \$300 000 | \$200 000 |

Note: Franchise fee is \$50 000 per year and 20% of gross profit is paid to Beautywise.

Explain **four **requirements for the new manager that Gemma should include in the job specification for a shop manager.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2020-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
Experience in jewellery retail **[K]**. The manager needs to know about selling rings and bracelets, as well as more expensive jewellery items that Gemma added after her first year **[Ap]**

Leadership skills **[K]**. The job specification should ask for someone who can motivate and manage the new employees in the shop **[Ap]**, making sure they work efficiently

Customer service skills **[K]**, as Gemma thinks excellent customer service is important **[Ap]**, so the manager must be able to provide this and teach it to new shop workers

Decision-making ability about inventory **[K]**. The manager will be responsible for choosing items to buy for the shop, so they need good judgement about which jewellery **[Ap] **will sell well

> 
>   - Experience - of selling jewellery
>   - Qualification/product knowledge - in retail management/gems
>   - Skills - e.g. Leadership skills – make sure new employees are well motived/communication skills – ensuring excellent customer service/ financial skills – make decision about which items of inventory to buy
>   - Trained – to operate the shop and supervise new employees
>   - Physical fitness – need to be on their feet all day in the shop
>   - Personal characteristics – friendly and welcoming to customers buying rings/easily approachable by customers when entering the new shop/able to speak the same language as local people in the area where the new shop is located
> - Application could include:
> 
>   - Operating the shop, making decisions about which items of inventory to buy, ensuring excellent customer service, ensuring new employees are motivated

> **[case-study]**

Keeping skilled managers who can effectively use delegation will help SRB continue to provide quality service **[An]**

Another factor to consider is the length of time managers have worked at SRB **[K]**. Choosing managers who haven't been with the company for long might be cheaper in terms of redundancy costs. This could help SRB reach its goal of saving \$1m in costs over the next two years **[Ap] **and pass these savings on to customers in the form of, for example, cheaper loans **[An]**
